commands_unrun.purpose: Find Microsoft.Azure.SignalR whose net8.0 implementation-library decoded string-literal use contains https://
Find Microsoft.Azure.SignalR with an exact Newtonsoft.Json dependency at declaration-edge depth 1, 2, or 3 for net8.0

rules.literal: library-literal is an eq predicate on decoded UTF-16 text. It matches an ordinal substring of each decoded string-literal use in the selected implementation libraries. Preserve operand whitespace, newlines, case, and all other text without normalization. The accepted length is 1 through 1024 UTF-16 code units. Identical repeats collapse to one operand, while distinct operands are incompatible. An empty listed values array is not an allow list: any text meeting these constraints is accepted. A 600-character astral Unicode operand requires 1200 UTF-16 code units and is rejected. library-literal and --tfm require each other; --tfm supplies one exact target framework and cannot be expressed as --where library-target=... . This predicate requires package-content acquisition and a package-content provider.
rules.dependency: Exact depends=Newtonsoft.Json with dependency-depth=3 is the preferred new syntax; eq matches direct dependencies and transitive declaration paths through the selected maximum of three edges. Without depth, exact depends matches direct dependencies only. depends-transitive=Newtonsoft.Json is the legacy spelling and matches only paths of depth 2 through the chosen maximum, so a direct-only dependency does not match it. dependency-depth accepts only 2, 3, or 4, and requires an exact depends predicate or legacy depends-transitive plus an explicit dependency-target TFM. dependency-target=all and depth 1 are invalid for the second command. A starts-with depends predicate remains direct and cannot alone satisfy the depth prerequisite. Repeated exact dependency terms are ANDed and share traversal. The selected facet does not specify further package-ID case or Unicode normalization rules, so none are assumed.
rules.candidate_vs_rows: For a Microsoft.Azure.* prefix population, set --take 5 to bound package candidates inspected and -n 2 to limit final result rows, for example argv ["dnx","dotnet-inspect","-y","--","package","query","Microsoft.Azure.*","--take","5","-n","2","--where","library-literal=https://","--tfm","net8.0","--json"]. The same bounds can be applied to a prefix dependency-depth query with its three --where predicates. Inspection predicates here admit at most five candidates; the exact package ID in the two main commands admits at most one. -n does not replace --take as the candidate-work bound.
